title: Fix the live pages engines fetch, not old training data
hypothesis: If we fix the PDP, facts page and reviews an engine actually cites, then a wrong AI answer corrects faster because retrieval reads the live page while training data barely moves.

signal.check: The prompt audit shows an engine quoting an old price, policy or spec, or missing a new SKU entirely.

expected_effect.size: unknown; one tracked case took about 2 years to move a training-data fact only partway

risk.note: Editing public fact pages is low risk; check nothing contradicts the brand record.

prerequisites: A prompt audit has already run
steps: Run the prompt audit and note any fact the engine states wrong or missing.
Find the live page the answer likely pulled that fact from: PDP, facts page, review site or a listicle.
Fix the fact on the site first, in plain text, not only in a PDF or image.
Update the same fact on every other channel that could feed the answer.

test.method: Rerun the same audit prompt after the fix, in a fresh session.
test.measure: Whether the answer now states the corrected fact.
test.read_point: Monthly, until the answer holds twice in a row.

title: Answer every sub-question a buyer prompt fans into on one page
hypothesis: If a collection page or buying guide answers the comparison, fit and objection questions a buyer prompt fans out into, then the page gets cited more because it fully answers the merged sub-queries an assistant runs.
does_not_apply_when: A single hero SKU with almost no comparison questions

signal.check: A collection page is a bare product grid, or a buying guide covers only the head term, while the target prompt is a buyer question like best X for Y.

expected_effect.size: unknown; sources report 9 to 11 fan-out sub-queries per prompt on average, up to 28

risk.note: Adding sections to an existing page rarely hurts; keep the page scannable.

prerequisites: List of the prompt's known sub-questions
steps: Run the target prompt and note the sub-questions the answer covers.
List the comparisons, fit, sizing and objection questions the prompt implies.
Add a short stand-alone section for each on the collection page or guide.
Recheck the live answer after publishing to see if coverage improved.

test.method: Compare the live answer's covered sub-questions before and after the rewrite.
test.measure: ai_citations, share of sub-questions answered on-page

title: Rank the exact page in Google and Bing top 10 before expecting AI citation
hypothesis: If we get the specific PDP or collection page into the top 10 organic results, then it appears in AI answers more often because assistants run background searches through the same search index.

signal.check: A page never shows up in AI answers even though the topic matches, and the exact URL does not rank in the top 10 for the same query.

expected_effect.size: reported overlap between Google top 10 and AI Overview citations ranges from about 38% to 76% depending on the study; treat as direction only

risk.note: Standard SEO work; no downside beyond time spent.

prerequisites: Target query and target URL identified
steps: Pick the query and the exact URL meant to answer it.
Check that URL's current rank in Google Search Console and in Bing.
If it is outside the top 10, run standard on-page and internal-link SEO on that page.
Recheck rank and the AI answer for the same query after the work.

test.method: Compare AI citation appearance before and after the page reaches the top 10.
test.read_point: 4 to 8 weeks after the page moves into the top 10

title: Report AI share of voice, never a single AI rank number
hypothesis: If the monthly report shows share of runs naming the brand per platform instead of a single rank, then the founder gets an honest picture because AI answers summarise many citations and vary run to run.

signal.check: A report or a tool shows a single AI rank or position column for the brand.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a reporting fix, not a growth lever on its own

risk.note: Reporting change only; no site or ad risk.

prerequisites: A frozen prompt set run 3 or more times per platform
steps: Remove any rank or position column from the AI visibility report.
Compute, per platform, the share of runs that name the brand.
Compute the share that cite the brand with a link.
Show both lines side by side each month.

test.method: Review the report format with the founder.

title: Pick 1 to 3 AI platforms from where buyers actually research
hypothesis: If we pick AI platforms from the checkout survey and referral data instead of a published ranking, then AEO effort concentrates on the platforms that actually influence this brand's buyers because platform overlap is low.
does_not_apply_when: No survey or referral data exists yet; start with ChatGPT and Google AI surfaces and revisit after one quarter

signal.check: An AEO plan names platforms before the checkout survey or GA4 AI channel has run for a quarter.

expected_effect.size: top-50 cited domain overlap across platforms measured at about 14%, so platform choice matters

risk.note: A wrong platform pick wastes effort but causes no direct harm.

prerequisites: Checkout survey with AI options running for at least one quarter
steps: Pull the checkout survey's AI-assistant answers and the GA4 AI channel referrer split.
Rank platforms by share of buyers who name them.
Weight the choice by the brand's AOV and consideration level.
Confirm or replace the platform list after one full quarter of data.

test.method: Compare the chosen platform list against survey results each quarter.

title: Split every mention report into named, cited and linked
hypothesis: If the AI visibility report separates named, cited with a link, and named but unlinked, then the founder sees the real value because only about 28% of AI mentions carry a link on average.

signal.check: A report shows a single citations number with no split for named versus linked.

expected_effect.size: about 28% of AI mentions carry a link on average, varying 10.7% to 51.6% by platform

prerequisites: A frozen prompt set with citations logged
steps: For each run, mark whether the brand is named, cited with a link, or both.
Compute the 3 shares separately per platform.
Add all 3 lines to the monthly report.
Flag any brand named with no PDP link as an impression, not a win.

test.method: Review the 3 lines each month for movement.

title: Make every brand fact match everywhere an engine can read it
hypothesis: If we make price, materials and return windows identical across the site, feed, directories and review platforms, then engines state the correct fact more often because they repeat what many sources agree on.

signal.check: The same SKU shows 2 different prices, materials or return windows on any channel an engine can read.

expected_effect.size: in one misinformation test, the official source was cited 84% of the time when it stated the specific fact clearly

risk.note: Correcting facts has no downside; check legal sign-off for claims.

steps: List every channel that states a brand fact: site, feed, marketplace, directories, reviews, schema.
Compare each fact against the verified fact sheet.
Fix the site version first, then every other channel.
Re-run a fact-check sweep quarterly or after any price or policy change.

test.method: Run a what do you know about brand prompt and mark each fact correct or wrong.
test.read_point: Monthly, and after any rebrand or price change

title: Chase brand and product mentions before backlinks
hypothesis: If off-site effort goes to earning product and brand mentions before link building, then AI visibility improves faster because branded mentions correlate more strongly with AI citation than backlinks do.

signal.check: Competitors get named in category AI answers and the store does not, while the off-site plan is mostly link building.

expected_effect.size: in one 75,000-brand vendor study, branded mention correlation with AI Overview visibility was 0.664, above backlinks and domain rating

risk.note: Reallocates effort; does not remove link building entirely.

prerequisites: Mention gap identified in the gap analysis
steps: Confirm the mention gap is the biggest gap from the 6-gap audit.
Rank off-site work: product and brand mentions first, links second.
Track product mentions on cited pages, not just brand mentions.
Re-check the mix monthly; do not drop link building for SEO entirely.

test.method: Compare mention count growth against link count growth over the quarter.

title: Judge the AI channel by order conversion and AOV, not traffic volume
hypothesis: If we compare AI-referred sessions against organic on conversion rate, AOV and revenue per session instead of raw traffic, then the founder judges the channel fairly because AI referral volume stays small for most stores.

signal.check: The GA4 AI channel has at least one month of data and someone is asking whether the AEO work pays off.

expected_effect.size: one vendor reported AI referrals at about 0.25% of traffic but 23 times its organic sign-up rate; treat as an example, not a target

steps: Pull AI-referred sessions, conversion rate, AOV and revenue per session from GA4.
Pull the same metrics for organic traffic over the same window.
Compare the two side by side, with session counts shown so a small base is visible.
Track the trend over 3 months, not a single month.

test.method: Trend the AI-vs-organic comparison for 3 consecutive months.

title: Recheck AI citations every month; they churn fast
hypothesis: If we re-run the same prompt set and log which URLs stay cited, then the AEO plan stays current because over 45% of AI Overview citations can change when the overview refreshes.

signal.check: No log exists showing whether a citation won last month is still live this month.

expected_effect.size: over 45% of AI Overview citations change when the overview refreshes, roughly every 2 days

prerequisites: A citation log spreadsheet or tracker
steps: Re-run the frozen prompt set monthly and log each cited URL.
Compare against last month's cited URLs for the same prompts.
Flag any URL that dropped out for review.
Run a deeper competitive audit each quarter on top of the monthly check.

test.method: Track months held per cited URL in the log.
test.read_point: Monthly, plus a quarterly deep audit

title: Do not budget on the idea that early AI visibility compounds
hypothesis: If we treat early AI visibility compounding through user memory as an unproven idea, then AEO budget is not overspent chasing a window that may not exist because no source has measured the effect.

signal.check: A vendor or internal plan argues for spending now before an early-mover window closes.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no measurement exists for this claim

risk.note: A budgeting caution, not a site change.

steps: When a plan cites early-mover compounding as a reason to spend now, ask for evidence.
Note that this claim is a hypothesis, not a measured result, in the plan document.
Keep spend tied to measured results (share of voice, conversion) instead.
Revisit the claim only if a source publishes real measurement.

test.method: None; this is a decision filter, not a testable tactic.
test.measure: Whether budget decisions cite measured results instead of this hypothesis

title: Keep the SEO budget and add AI search spend on top of it
hypothesis: If AEO spend is added on top of the existing SEO budget instead of replacing it, then organic revenue holds while the AI channel grows because classic SEO still delivers most of what AI answers need.

signal.check: A search is dying headline or a vendor pitch proposes moving SEO budget into AEO.

expected_effect.size: one source estimates classic SEO delivers about 80% of what AEO needs

risk.note: Cutting SEO spend to fund AEO risks the larger, proven organic revenue channel.

steps: Confirm current SEO budget and its recent organic revenue trend.
Add any new AEO spend as a separate line item, not a reallocation.
Track organic revenue from PDP and collection pages monthly while AEO work runs.
Flag any drop in organic revenue coinciding with a budget shift for review.

test.method: Compare organic revenue before and after AEO spend is added.

title: Rank for your category terms first; that is most of the AEO job
hypothesis: If we get collection and product pages ranking for their category terms before running AEO-specific tactics, then AI visibility follows more easily because 70% to 80% of AEO effort is really SEO.
does_not_apply_when: The brand already ranks in the top 10 for its main category terms

signal.check: Collection and category pages do not yet rank in the top 10 for their category terms.

expected_effect.size: sources estimate 70% to 80% of the AEO job is standard SEO

steps: Check current rank for each collection page's category terms.
Prioritise SEO fixes on pages ranking outside the top 10.
Run this before any AEO-only tactic like Reddit or listicle outreach.
Recheck ranking monthly.

test.method: Track top-10 coverage for category terms over time.

title: Run a new AEO engagement in a fixed order: crawlers, measurement, gaps, fix
hypothesis: If day 1 covers a crawler check, then measurement setup, then a gap analysis, then the single biggest gap's fix, then no later work is wasted on a blocked or unmeasured store.

signal.check: AEO work is starting on a store with no prior robots.txt check, no AI measurement and no gap analysis.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a sequencing fix, not a metric mover on its own

steps: Run the 30-second robots.txt crawler check first.
Set up the GA4 AI channel and the checkout survey question next.
Run the gap analysis once measurement is live.
Fix the single biggest gap before moving to the next.

test.method: Confirm each step's deliverable exists before the next step starts.

title: Choose AI platforms from survey and referral data, not a published ranking
hypothesis: If platform choice waits for the checkout survey and referral data instead of a published consumer ranking, then effort lands on the platforms this brand's own buyers actually use.

signal.check: A plan names AI platforms to prioritise before the checkout survey has run.

expected_effect.size: unknown; published rankings vary widely by source and audience

steps: Read the checkout survey's AI-assistant answers.
Read the GA4 AI channel referral split by platform.
If neither exists yet, start with ChatGPT and Google AI surfaces as a placeholder.
Replace the placeholder list once a quarter of real data exists.

test.method: Compare the placeholder platform list against real survey data after one quarter.

title: Spend content hours on transactional pages before what is X articles
hypothesis: If content hours go to PDP, collection, comparison and use-case pages before broad informational articles, then the content budget produces more orders because AI Overviews already answer most broad questions.
does_not_apply_when: A brand with real category authority and a genuinely new point of view

signal.check: A small or mid-size store's content plan is mostly informational blog posts, not transactional pages.

expected_effect.size: AI Overviews appear on about 21% of keywords but 58% of question queries; most informational clicks are already absorbed

risk.note: Reallocates writing hours; no site risk.

steps: Audit the content calendar's share of hours by page type.
Move hours toward PDP, collection, comparison and use-case pages.
Keep informational pieces only where the AI filter shows a real click opportunity.
Recheck the content hour split quarterly.

test.method: Track conversion rate and revenue from new transactional pages versus new informational pages.

title: Target narrow buyer prompts when bigger brands own the head term
hypothesis: If we narrow the target prompt by size, material, use case or budget instead of chasing the head term, then the store gets cited faster because the chat tail is bigger and mostly unanswered.

signal.check: 3 to 4 larger brands are already named for best category and the store is not.

expected_effect.size: one source reports a new brand can be cited within days for a specific question nobody has answered

risk.note: Competitors may copy a working niche once it shows results; keep finding new narrow angles.

prerequisites: Catalog attributes that support real narrow use cases
steps: List the catalog's genuine narrow use cases: size, material, use case, fit, budget.
Build or rewrite a page or FAQ answer for each narrow prompt.
Check share of voice on the narrow prompts after one month.
Move to a new narrow angle once a competitor copies a working one.

test.method: Run the narrow prompts monthly and track brand naming.

title: Work the tail and mentions as a small brand; defend the head as a big one
hypothesis: If a small store puts effort into tail prompts and mentions instead of the head prompt, then it earns citations sooner because head prompts go to high-authority pages while tail prompts have no authority gate yet.
does_not_apply_when: An established brand that already holds strong domain authority in its category

signal.check: Deciding whether to spend AEO budget chasing the best category prompt.

expected_effect.size: one vendor study puts the median domain rating of ChatGPT's top-cited pages at 90, well above most small stores

risk.note: Strategic choice; no direct site risk.

steps: Check the store's domain authority relative to the category's head-prompt winners.
If well behind, commit the quarter's budget to tail prompts and mentions instead.
Test 1 head prompt each quarter to see whether the field is closing.
Shift budget toward the head prompt only once test results show real movement.

test.method: Track share of voice on 1 head prompt each quarter as a canary.

title: Put rewrite budget on your 5 to 10 highest-traffic pages, not the whole catalog
hypothesis: If the AEO rewrite budget concentrates on the 5 to 10 pages that already earn traffic or links, then the biggest citation gains land fastest because about 1 in 20 pages typically drive most of a site's traffic.
does_not_apply_when: A hero-SKU store, which should instead rewrite only its 1 to 2 core pages

signal.check: A plan says rewrite the catalog instead of naming specific priority pages.

expected_effect.size: one source reports about 1 in 20 landing pages drive about 85% of traffic

prerequisites: Traffic and backlink report for the catalog
steps: Sort pages by traffic and referring domains.
Pick the top 5 to 10 for a wide catalog, or the top 1 to 2 for a hero-SKU store.
Build the catalog citation priority list before writing any brief.
Do not start new page rewrites outside this list until it is done.

test.method: Track citations and traffic on the priority list versus the rest of the catalog.
test.read_point: 8 to 12 weeks after the rewrite round

title: Screen every AEO tactic by time horizon and shopper benefit
hypothesis: If every proposed tactic is screened by the brand's time horizon and whether it gives the shopper the best answer, then risky tactics get caught early because a Google penalty can suppress a domain for 2 to 3 years.

signal.check: A vendor pitch or an internal idea proposes a tactic from section 3.10 of this playbook or anything similar.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a risk filter, not a growth lever

risk.note: A decision filter; the risk it prevents is in the tactic, not in this step.

steps: For any proposed tactic, write down the brand's time horizon (short-term site or long-term brand).
Write down whether the tactic gives the shopper the best answer or games the system.
Reject any tactic that fails either test, regardless of promised upside.
Log the decision and reasoning for future reference.

test.method: None; this is a gate, not a testable tactic.
test.measure: Whether every proposed tactic has a written horizon and shopper-benefit answer
test.read_point: Before any new tactic is approved

title: Fix the product or review page when the AI answer is bad, not the mentions plan
lever: root cause fix for bad description
hypothesis: If a negative or wrong AI description traces to a low-rated review platform, then fixing the product or the review page corrects the answer because no listicle or Reddit work fixes a real quality problem.

signal.check: The prompt audit shows a negative or wrong AI answer and the cited source is a review platform with a low rating.

expected_effect.size: unknown; depends on the underlying product or service issue

risk.note: Routes the fix to the right team instead of wasting mention effort.

prerequisites: Access to the cited review platform's data
steps: Identify the review platform the AI answer cites for a negative description.
Check that platform's current rating and read the negative reviews for real product issues.
Route real product faults to the product and returns team.
Once fixed, run the neutral review request on the platform the engine cites.

test.method: Track the cited platform's rating and rerun the audit prompt monthly.

title: Split AEO ownership: pages to the SEO owner, video and community to a community marketer
hypothesis: If on-site AEO work stays with the SEO or store owner while video and community work goes to a community-minded marketer, then both areas get done well because the two skill sets rarely overlap.
does_not_apply_when: A solo founder doing all the work; the split does not apply until a second person joins

signal.check: 2 or more people share AEO work and it is not clear who owns video, Reddit or listicle outreach.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a staffing fix, not a metric mover

prerequisites: More than 1 person working on AEO
steps: List the citation groups: own site, video, UGC, tier-1 affiliates, tier-2 affiliates, blogs.
Assign a named owner per group.
Keep on-site page work with the SEO or store owner.
Assign video and community threads to a community-minded marketer.

test.method: Confirm each group has a named owner on the mention target list.
test.read_point: At team setup and after any staffing change

title: Put seasonal AEO pages and mentions live weeks before the peak
hypothesis: If gift guides, holiday collection pages and seasonal listicle outreach go live weeks before a sales peak instead of on the normal refresh cadence, then the store gets cited during the peak because citations take time to appear.

signal.check: The promo calendar shows a holiday, back-to-school or launch spike with no AEO row.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source measures a seasonal AEO lift, this is general practice

prerequisites: Promo calendar with known peak dates
steps: Mark every seasonal sales spike on the promo calendar.
Add an AEO row with page-live and outreach dates weeks ahead of each spike.
Publish seasonal collection pages, gift guides and listicle pitches on that earlier date.
Verify against the brand's own past seasonal data before finalising the lead time.

test.method: Compare AI-referred sessions during the peak against the prior season.
test.read_point: During and after the peak window

title: Let AOV decide how much content and mention budget each page type gets
hypothesis: If a low-AOV catalog spends on collection pages and reviews while a high-AOV catalog spends on buying guides and comparison pages, then content budget matches how each buyer segment actually decides.

signal.check: Content and mention budget is split across the catalog with no AOV-based rule.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source uses AOV as a variable, this is general practice

prerequisites: AOV band known per product line
steps: Split the catalog into low-AOV, impulse items and high-AOV, considered items.
Send low-AOV budget to collection pages, review collection and volume plays.
Send high-AOV budget to buying guides, comparison pages and original data.
Recheck the split when AOV shifts across a product line.

test.method: Track content output and citation rate per AOV band.

title: Check buyer country and device mix before copying a US AI platform ranking
hypothesis: If GA4 shows most buyers are outside the US or mostly on mobile, then platform priority should come from that data instead of a US-centric published ranking, because regional assistants and review platforms may differ.

signal.check: GA4 shows buyers outside the US or mostly on mobile devices.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source in this playbook covers non-US or mobile-first markets

steps: Pull the GA4 country and device split for the brand's buyers.
If most buyers are outside the US or mobile-first, do not assume the US platform ranking applies.
Add a survey question on which assistants and apps local buyers actually use.
Fix the platform list only after this local data comes in.

test.method: Compare local survey responses against the assumed platform list.

title: Check robots.txt for AI crawler blocks on day 1 and after every platform change
hypothesis: If robots.txt is checked for AI crawler blocks before any other AEO work and after every theme, app or CDN change, then downstream work is not wasted because a blocked crawler stops everything after it.

signal.check: No recent robots.txt check exists, or a theme, app, CDN or platform change happened since the last check.

expected_effect.size: about 5.9% of 140 million sites scanned block GPTBot

risk.note: A read-only check; changes only happen if a block is found.

steps: Open yourdomain.com/robots.txt in a browser.
List every User-agent block and its Disallow lines.
Check for rules against GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and PerplexityBot.
Repeat this check after every theme, app, CDN or platform change.

test.method: Re-fetch robots.txt after any fix and confirm the block is gone.
test.read_point: Day 1 and after every platform change

title: Allow search and citation bots, decide on training bots, keep checkout blocked
hypothesis: If robots.txt allows citation bots on PDP and collection pages while keeping cart, checkout and account paths blocked, then the store is retrievable without forfeiting the channel or exposing private paths.

signal.check: Robots.txt policy for AI bots is being set, or a legal or brand owner asks to block AI entirely.

expected_effect.size: unknown; blocking everything forfeits the channel entirely

risk.note: Editing robots.txt incorrectly could expose private paths; keep a backup.

prerequisites: Current crawler names and training-vs-search split confirmed
steps: List each vendor's search bot and training bot separately.
Allow search and citation bots on public catalog and content paths.
Decide the brand's training-bot policy separately and apply it.
Keep existing disallow rules on cart, checkout and account paths.

test.method: Re-fetch robots.txt and confirm citation bots appear in server logs on priority pages.
test.read_point: After deploying the policy and monthly after

title: Check your Cloudflare AI-bot setting on its own
hypothesis: If the Cloudflare AI-bot setting is checked separately from robots.txt, then a silent rewrite is caught because Cloudflare's default can disallow AI crawlers without the owner knowing.

signal.check: The store sits behind Cloudflare, including a setup an agency built, with no recent check of its AI-bot feature.

expected_effect.size: unknown; Cloudflare's default setting changes without notice

risk.note: A configuration check; verify current UI before changing.

steps: Open the Cloudflare bot settings and find the AI-bot robots.txt feature.
Check whether it is on and rewriting robots.txt to block AI crawlers.
Turn it off or edit the managed rules if the brand wants to be cited.
Re-fetch robots.txt from outside after any Cloudflare change.

test.method: Fetch robots.txt from outside the network after the change.

title: Confirm every SKU and collection page is indexed in Google and Bing
hypothesis: If every SKU and collection page is confirmed indexed in both Google and Bing, then more pages become eligible for AI citation because an unindexed page cannot be surfaced by either engine.

signal.check: A new page never appears in AI answers, or the store just launched or added a collection with no sitemap submission.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a page not indexed cannot be cited at all

prerequisites: Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools access
steps: Submit the sitemap to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
Spot-check indexing with a site:yourdomain.com search.
Compare indexed counts against the sitemap's page count in both consoles.
Resubmit at launch, at every new collection, and whenever a page never appears in answers.

test.method: Compare indexed counts in both consoles against the sitemap.
test.read_point: At launch, every new collection, and monthly after

title: Put product copy, specs and FAQ text in raw HTML, not JS-only
hypothesis: If product copy, specs, reviews and FAQ text render in raw HTML instead of only after JavaScript runs, then AI crawlers can read and cite the content because some crawlers do not render JavaScript.

signal.check: The theme or an app injects review widgets, size charts or spec blocks client-side with JavaScript.

expected_effect.size: unknown; one source claims OpenAI's crawler does not render JavaScript while others do

risk.note: Server-side rendering changes are generally safe if tested first.

steps: Disable JavaScript in the browser and reload the top pages.
Check that title, meta description, headings, body copy, specs and FAQ still show.
For any missing block, move it to server-side rendering or pre-rendering.
Retest with JS disabled after the fix.

test.method: Reload the top pages with JavaScript disabled and confirm all fact blocks show.
test.read_point: After the fix and at every future theme or app change

title: Keep PDP and collection pages fast enough to pass Core Web Vitals
hypothesis: If PDP and collection pages pass Core Web Vitals, then they are less likely to be skipped before being scored, because a slow page can be dropped by a crawler before it is read.

signal.check: Core Web Vitals fail on the store's money pages.

expected_effect.size: unknown; the speed engineering work itself lives in the site-speed domain

steps: Run Lighthouse on the top 10 pages by traffic.
Identify the largest single cause of failing Core Web Vitals.
Hand the fix to the site-speed workstream.
Recheck Core Web Vitals after the fix.

test.method: Re-run Lighthouse on the same pages after the fix.
test.read_point: After the fix, then every 28 days for field data

title: Give every cited page one H1 that states what is sold
hypothesis: If every page meant to be cited has exactly 1 H1 stating what it sells, followed by a clean H2 and H3 tree, then engines chunk and cite the content more accurately because a chunk boundary can fall at any heading.

signal.check: A theme uses the logo or brand name as the H1, or a PDP has no heading structure below the title.

expected_effect.size: unknown; heading structure is a foundational fix

risk.note: Template change; check other pages using the same theme.

steps: Crawl the top pages and check the current heading hierarchy.
Fix any page with the logo as H1 or with multiple H1 tags.
Set 1 H1 stating what is sold, then H2 sections and H3 subsections.
Recheck the heading crawl after the theme fix.

test.method: Re-run a headings crawl on the top pages.

title: Keep Product, Offer and review schema accurate and validated
hypothesis: If Product, Offer, Organization and review schema stay accurate and validated on every important page, then shoppable answer cards and rich results reflect the real product because they read this data directly.

signal.check: A vendor proposes a schema project as an AEO lever, or a schema app was installed and never checked.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no confirmed evidence schema alone improves AI citation, but it matters for shoppable commerce answers

risk.note: Validation only fixes existing schema, no new risk.

steps: Run a schema validator on the hero PDP and 1 collection page.
Compare every schema fact against the fact sheet.
Fix any mismatch or invalid field.
Repeat validation after every app change.

test.method: Re-run the validator after every app change.
test.read_point: After every app or theme change

title: Put llms.txt at the bottom of the technical fix list
hypothesis: If engineering time skips llms.txt until a major engine documents reading it, then hours go to fixes that matter now, because no major engine currently confirms using it.

signal.check: A developer or vendor proposes building an llms.txt file as a priority AEO task.

expected_effect.size: unknown; adoption is unconfirmed as of this playbook's date

risk.note: A prioritisation decision, no direct risk.

steps: When llms.txt is proposed, check current adoption by major engines.
Deprioritise it below crawler access, JS rendering and indexing fixes.
Recheck adoption quarterly.
Treat a vendor who leads with llms.txt as a caution sign, not a reason to prioritise it.

test.method: Recheck vendor documentation quarterly for confirmed adoption.

title: Redirect made-up product URLs that AI answers send shoppers to
hypothesis: If invented product or collection URLs from AI answers get redirected to the closest real page, then AI-referred visitors reach a real page instead of a dead end, recovering lost conversion.

signal.check: The GA4 AI channel's landing-page report shows repeat visits to a 404 page.

expected_effect.size: AI sends visitors to 404 pages about 2.87 times more often than Google in one vendor's data

risk.note: A 301 redirect is low risk and reversible.

steps: Filter GA4 for AI-referrer sessions landing on 404 pages.
Identify any invented SKU or collection URL getting steady visits.
301 redirect it to the closest real PDP or collection page.
Recheck monthly for new AI-referred 404s.

test.method: Track AI-referred 404 sessions before and after the redirect.

title: Host FAQ, care and policy pages in a subdirectory, not an isolated subdomain
hypothesis: If FAQ, care, sizing and policy pages move from a subdomain or help-desk tool into a subdirectory of the main domain and cross-link, then they earn citation credit more easily because subdomains and isolated articles underperform for citation.

signal.check: The help centre sits on a subdomain or inside a help-desk tool with no links between articles.

expected_effect.size: unknown; the source claims subdomains underperform without a figure

risk.note: Moving domains risks broken links; set up redirects carefully.

prerequisites: Verify whether the help-desk platform supports subdirectory hosting
steps: Check whether the current help-desk platform can host under a subdirectory.
Move or mirror FAQ, care, sizing and policy pages under the main domain.
Cross-link related help articles to each other.
Link each help page to the PDP or collection it supports.

test.method: Track indexing and citations for help pages before and after the move.

title: Link every guide, FAQ and comparison page to the product it sells for
hypothesis: If every guide, FAQ and comparison page links to the PDP or collection it supports, then AI-referred guide traffic converts more often because the visitor is 1 click from buying.

signal.check: A guide or FAQ page earns AI clicks but produces no orders, and it has no link to a money page.

expected_effect.size: unknown; internal links help navigation and conversion but no figure is given

steps: List every guide, FAQ and comparison page.
Check whether each links to its relevant PDP or collection.
Add the link where it fits naturally, not on every mention.
Link back from the money page to the guide where useful.

test.method: Compare conversion rate on guide traffic before and after adding links.

title: Map the catalog to one page per distinct product and useful collection
hypothesis: If the catalog is mapped to 1 dedicated page per distinct product and per collection with real demand, then AI answers cite the right specific page instead of a generic one covering too much.

signal.check: A new store build or re-platform is starting with no page-per-offering map, or 1 page currently covers many products.

expected_effect.size: unknown; covering every product on 1 page is called the number 1 mistake by one source

risk.note: Planning task; execution risk is in the build itself.

steps: List every distinct product and every collection with independent demand.
Confirm demand for each variant before building a dedicated page for it.
Use a consistent URL pattern across the mapped pages.
Build the site map before writing any page content.

test.method: Check the site map covers every product and collection with real demand.

title: Keep the merchant feed accurate; shoppable AI cards read from it
hypothesis: If the Shopping or Merchant Center feed always matches the PDP's price and stock, then shoppable AI answer cards show correct information because they draw on feed and rich-snippet data.

signal.check: A price, stock level or title changes on the PDP but not in the product feed.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no ecommerce source measures the effect of feed accuracy on AI shoppable cards

steps: Compare feed price and availability against the PDP for the top 20 SKUs weekly.
Fix any mismatch found.
Set an alert or scheduled check for feed drift.
Confirm the fix reflects in the feed within a day.

test.method: Weekly spot check of feed versus PDP for top SKUs.

title: Give every SKU a canonical URL and keep filter pages out of the index
hypothesis: If every SKU has 1 canonical URL and filtered collection pages stay out of the index, then AI crawlers cite the right page instead of a duplicate or a filtered variant.

signal.check: A product has size, colour or bundle variants, or a collection page has filters generating many URLs.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source covers SKU-level canonical handling directly

steps: Crawl the site and list every product's variant URLs.
Set 1 canonical URL per product, keeping variants on that page or splitting only where demand is proven.
Add noindex or canonical tags to filtered collection URLs.
Re-crawl to confirm 1 indexable URL per product and no indexed filter pages.

test.method: Re-crawl the site after the fix.

title: Treat an out-of-stock or discontinued page as a citation risk, not only a sales one
hypothesis: If the availability and price fact updates the same day a SKU sells out or is discontinued, then an AI answer does not repeat a stale fact, because engines repeat whatever they last read.

signal.check: A SKU sells out, is discontinued or goes on backorder.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source covers inventory status as an AI citation risk directly

steps: Update the PDP availability field the same day a SKU changes status.
Update the schema and product feed to match.
Note the discontinued or backorder status clearly in the fact block.
Check the audit prompt for that SKU to confirm the answer reflects the change.

test.method: Rerun a fact audit on a recently out-of-stock SKU.
test.read_point: Within a week of the status change

title: Open every page section with a direct answer under a question heading
hypothesis: If every PDP, collection and guide section opens with a 20 to 50 word direct answer under a question-shaped heading, then engines lift a clean answer more often because this is the one rule every source agrees on.

signal.check: A page opens with a brand story, a slogan or a bare spec table instead of a direct answer.

expected_effect.size: one source claims over 44% of AI citations come from the first third of a page; unsourced

risk.note: Rewriting an opening section is low risk.

steps: Pick the pages meant to be cited: PDP, category, buying guide, comparison, FAQ.
Write a 20 to 50 word direct answer for each section's heading.
Put the answer immediately under the heading, before any brand story.
Read the first 50 words of each section and confirm it answers the heading alone.

test.method: Reread the first 50 words of each rewritten section.

title: Make each fact block on a page stand alone
hypothesis: If each fact block reads as a complete answer with no reference back to earlier text, then engines cite it correctly because they chunk pages at heading boundaries the writer cannot see.

signal.check: A spec section says as above, this item or see our policy instead of stating the fact directly.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no numeric result reported, source-level claim only

risk.note: Editing existing copy for clarity is low risk.

steps: Read each fact block out of context, as if it were the only thing shown.
Rewrite any block that depends on earlier text to state the fact directly.
Keep brand voice in the intro and story sections, not the fact blocks.
Re-check every fact block reads as a complete answer alone.

test.method: Re-read each fact block in isolation after the rewrite.

title: Name the product and material; never say this item or many users
hypothesis: If copy names the product, material and model number instead of vague pronouns, then engines extract a clean, correctly attributed answer because the sentence needs no earlier context to make sense.

signal.check: Copy uses this item, this product or many users in place of the actual name.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a writing quality fix with no measured figure

steps: Search the fact blocks for this product, this item and many users.
Replace each with the specific product, material, model number or competitor SKU named.
Keep 1 idea per sentence, subject-verb-object.
If a sentence needs 2 reads, simplify it.

test.method: Search rewritten copy for the banned vague phrases.

title: Write titles, H1s and openers in the shopper's own words
hypothesis: If titles, H1s and opening lines use the shopper's real phrasing from prompts, tickets and search terms instead of trade jargon, then the page matches more real queries because engines often phrase sub-queries differently from the trade term.

signal.check: A rewrite brief is being written with no source phrase attached to each heading.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no measured figure, direction only

prerequisites: Real buyer phrasing from support tickets, search queries or survey free text
steps: Pull real buyer phrasing from support tickets, search terms and survey free text.
Pick 1 primary phrase per page, in the buyer's own words, not the trade term.
Use it in the title tag, URL slug, H1 and first sentence.
Note the source phrase beside each heading in the brief.

test.method: Compare click-through and citation rate for pages using buyer phrasing versus trade terms.

title: Refresh high-intent pages every 2 months with real new facts
hypothesis: If category, comparison and top guide pages get a substantive refresh every 2 months with new prices, specs and picks, then citation odds improve because cited content runs about 25.7% fresher than typical organic results.

signal.check: A money page has not changed in 2 months, or a plan proposes lengthening a page instead of refreshing it.

expected_effect.size: cited content measured about 25.7% fresher than organic results in one vendor study across 174,000+ pages

steps: List category, comparison and top guide pages by last real update date.
For any page over 2 months old, update prices, specs, examples and recommendations.
Move the visible date only when the content actually changed.
Never let a page sit untouched past 6 months.

test.method: Track citation and impression changes after each refresh.

title: Refresh a page with existing links and falling traffic before writing a new one
hypothesis: If a page with existing backlinks and declining traffic gets refreshed before any new page is written, then citations come back faster because freshness plus prior authority beats starting from zero.

signal.check: Search Console shows pages sliding in traffic, and the content gap is the biggest gap from the audit.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no numeric result reported, direction only

risk.note: Keep the previous version in case the refresh underperforms.

prerequisites: Top-pages report with traffic change and referring domains
steps: Sort top pages by traffic decline while keeping ones with real referring domains.
Drop pages whose main problem is thin links; a rewrite will not fix them.
Refresh the keepers with new facts, prices and an answer-first opening.
Request indexing and add the page's prompts to the test set.

test.method: Track impressions and citations within 2 months of the refresh.

title: Build the page format that already wins the target prompt
hypothesis: If a page is built as the format already winning the target prompt, such as a comparison table or a listicle, then it earns citation more easily because AI answers favor formats that already dominate that prompt.

signal.check: A brief is being written and nobody has checked which page type currently wins the target prompt's citations.

expected_effect.size: 43.8% of citations in one platform's answers were listicles or comparisons in one vendor study

prerequisites: Live answer check for the target prompt
steps: Run the target prompt and note the page type winning citations: grid, table, listicle or article.
Build the page as that winning format.
Put a comparison table near the top if that is the winning format.
Note the chosen format in the brief.

test.method: Recheck the live answer's citations after publishing the matched format.

title: Publish honest comparison pages against 3 to 4 bigger rivals
hypothesis: If an honest brand-versus-competitor page with a table near the top and current prices goes live for 3 to 4 named larger rivals, then engines have real reasoning to recommend the brand because the comparison supplies the answer directly.
does_not_apply_when: A luxury or considered-purchase brand where naming a cheaper rival can hurt the position

signal.check: Shoppers in this category compare alternatives and no honest comparison page exists yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no measured figure, source claim only

risk.note: Naming a competitor can also lift that competitor's own visibility; choose deliberately.

prerequisites: Approved competitor claims and legal review process
steps: Pick 3 to 4 competitors larger than the brand that appear in the category's AI answers.
Build a table first: features, materials, price, shipping, warranty, best for.
Write honest pros and cons for both sides.
Get legal sign-off on every comparative claim before publishing.
Refresh prices and specs every 2 months.

test.method: Recheck the comparison prompt's citations after publishing.

title: Replace vague claims with real numbers, quotes and test data
hypothesis: If a buying guide or PDP replaces words like premium and best with real numbers, named quotes and the brand's own test data, then the page earns more trust and citation because it says something no competitor page says.

signal.check: A buying guide or PDP spec section uses premium, durable or best with no figure behind it.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no measured figure, source recommendation only

risk.note: Only publish real, verifiable figures; never invent original data.

prerequisites: Real test, survey or return-reason data the brand actually holds
steps: Find every vague claim in a buying guide or PDP spec section.
Trace it to real data in the brand record, or gather real data if none exists.
Replace the vague claim with the number, named quote or linked source.
Verify every number traces back to the brand record before publishing.

test.method: Audit the published page for any claim without a traceable source.
test.read_point: Before publishing, then recheck citations after

title: Add one first-hand fact to every page before publishing
hypothesis: If every page competing for a citation includes at least 1 first-hand fact no competitor page has, then it survives the information-gain test engines increasingly apply, because scored-to-match content gets discounted.

signal.check: A page is ready to publish and nobody has asked what it says that no competitor page says.

expected_effect.size: unknown; source recommendation only

steps: Before publishing, ask what this page says that no competitor page says.
If nothing, add a fit note, a wear test, a real customer question or a documented result.
Confirm the fact is real and traceable to the brand record.
Add it to the page before it goes live.

test.method: Track citation rate for pages with a first-hand fact versus those without.

title: Publish a facts page that answers every gap the prompt audit found
hypothesis: If a facts page publishes the specific price, shipping, returns, materials and founding year the prompt audit shows an engine guessing, then engines state the correct answer instead of inventing one, because engines pick specific fiction over vague or absent truth.

signal.check: The prompt audit shows an engine guessing a price, a return window or a founding year.

expected_effect.size: in one misinformation test, the official source was cited 84% of the time once it stated the fact clearly

risk.note: Publishing true facts is low risk.

steps: List every gap the prompt audit found: price, shipping, returns, materials, years trading.
Publish an About or Facts page stating each fact clearly.
Use this page as the canonical source for schema and directories too.
Map every audit gap to a page that now states the fact.

test.method: Rerun the audit prompt after publishing.

title: Keep facts identical across site, schema, feed, directories and reviews
hypothesis: If name, address, prices, facts and claims stay identical across every channel an engine reads, then the consensus signal strengthens because repeating the same entities across channels builds trust in the answer.

signal.check: A rebrand, move, price change or new certification happened and channels have not been checked for consistency.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no numeric figure given, source claim only

steps: List every channel: site, schema, feed, directories, review platforms, listicles, video descriptions.
Run a quarterly fact sweep comparing each channel against the fact sheet.
Fix any mismatch found.
Re-audit immediately after any rebrand, move, price change or new certification.

test.method: Quarterly fact sweep across every listed channel.
test.read_point: Quarterly, and after any rebrand or price change

title: Cap the FAQ at 5 questions on a PDP or collection page
hypothesis: If a PDP or collection page keeps its FAQ to about 5 real buyer questions and sends the rest to a buying guide, then the money page keeps its transactional focus instead of diluting it with a long Q&A block.

signal.check: A PDP carries 10 or more FAQ items, or a collection page has none at all.

expected_effect.size: unknown; source recommends a 5-item cap with no measured figure

prerequisites: Question research export with page-type routing
steps: Count the current FAQ items on each PDP and collection page.
Keep the 5 most-asked fit, sizing, shipping and returns questions.
Move the remaining questions to a buying guide or blog piece.
Link the guide from the FAQ section for buyers who want more.

test.method: Compare conversion rate before and after trimming the FAQ.

title: Make every PDP and category page pass the 2-second test
hypothesis: If a shopper can tell what the page sells, and what to do next, within 2 seconds without scrolling, then more visitors convert because a confusing first fold loses both shoppers and citation-worthy clarity.

signal.check: The first fold shows a slogan or a lifestyle image with no product name, price or button.

expected_effect.size: unknown; general usability finding, no ecommerce figure given

risk.note: Layout change; test before full rollout.

steps: Load the page without scrolling and note what a first-time visitor sees.
Confirm plain headline, real product photo, price and add-to-cart or CTA are all visible.
Set 1 primary keyword per page, with secondary terms in subheadings.
Run a 5-person first-fold test on mobile.

test.method: Run a 5-person first-fold test on mobile before and after the change.

title: Cover a topic end to end, but keep each intent on its own page type
hypothesis: If a topic cluster runs from how to choose through buy but each intent gets its own page type, then more entry points exist without diluting any single page, because a collection page and a guide serve different intents.

signal.check: A topic cluster is being planned with no clear mapping from intent to page type.

expected_effect.size: unknown; direction only, no measured figure

steps: Map the topic's intents from informational through transactional.
Put the collection page at the transactional end of the map first.
Add an informational guide only if the AI filter shows the Overview does not already answer it fully.
Confirm the cluster map has a transactional page before any guide.

test.method: Check whether the informational piece earns clicks the Overview did not already absorb.

title: Give a proprietary material or method its own brand name
hypothesis: If a proprietary material, fit system or process gets a brand name defined on the site and repeated everywhere, then engines attribute the idea to the brand instead of flattening it into unattributed general knowledge.
does_not_apply_when: No proprietary material, sizing method or process exists yet

signal.check: The brand has its own material, sizing method or process with no brand name attached.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim with no measured figure

steps: Identify any proprietary material, fit system or process the brand owns.
Give it a clear brand name.
Define it on the site first, in a dedicated section.
Repeat the named term consistently in video, social, community and press.

test.method: Ask an AI engine about the named method and check whether it attributes it to the brand.
test.read_point: 8 to 12 weeks after defining and repeating the name

title: Write long buying guides 60% to 70% in short answer capsules
hypothesis: If a long buying guide is written 60% to 70% in short answer capsules and the rest in prose, then it is easier for an engine to lift a clean answer while still reading naturally to a human.

signal.check: A long guide is being planned or exists as mostly narrative prose with few standalone answer sections.

expected_effect.size: heuristic from 1 source, attributed to an unverifiable peer-reviewed study; use as a starting ratio, not a law

steps: Draft the guide's outline with each section marked capsule or prose.
Aim for 60% to 70% of sections in short answer capsule form.
Keep the rest as prose for narrative flow and brand voice.
Count the capsule share in the brief before finalizing.

test.method: Count capsule share per guide in the brief before publishing.

title: Draft with AI, add first-hand detail, edit by hand, never bulk-publish
hypothesis: If every AI-drafted page gets a first-hand fact injected and a human edit before publishing, and pages never get bulk-published, then the site avoids a rank-and-tank penalty because Google penalizes thin scaled content, not AI authorship itself.

signal.check: Content is being produced with AI assistance, or a vendor proposes producing hundreds of SKU descriptions quickly.

expected_effect.size: sites that scaled from about 100 to 1,000+ posts in weeks saw a spike then a decline, with 2 to 3 year recoveries in one observed case

risk.note: Bulk-publishing thin AI content risks a lasting ranking penalty; treat this as a hard rule, not a suggestion.

prerequisites: Brand brief and fact sheet available to the drafting workflow
steps: Draft the page with AI assistance using the brand brief and fact sheet.
Inject at least 1 first-hand product detail the assistant could not know.
Edit every draft by hand and verify every fact and link.
Never publish more than a small, reviewed batch of pages at once.

test.method: Track ranking and traffic trend after any content batch, watching for a spike-then-decline pattern.
test.read_point: 3 to 6 months after any content batch

title: Copy the structure that performs, never the copy, when scaling pages
hypothesis: If a page's proven structure gets replicated across the catalog with fresh copy on each page, then the whole catalog benefits from what works without creating duplicate content that hurts ranking.

signal.check: 1 page shows citations or a real lift and the rest of the catalog is waiting on a template.

expected_effect.size: unknown; source recommendation only

risk.note: Template reuse is safe as long as copy is not duplicated.

prerequisites: 1 page already showing a citation or performance lift
steps: Document the winning page's structure: section order, capsule placement, table format.
Apply the same structure to other catalog pages.
Write fresh copy for each page; never repeat a paragraph across PDPs.
Keep meta descriptions under about 150 characters with the page's primary term.

test.method: Check no 2 PDPs share a paragraph, and track citation rate across the scaled pages.

title: Put plan terms and cancellation policy in the same fact blocks as price
hypothesis: If plan terms, cancellation policy and billing cadence sit right next to the price on a subscription PDP, then engines answer cancellation questions correctly instead of treating the gap as a trust problem the way a missing return policy would be treated.

signal.check: The store sells a plan or a refill and the PDP states price with no cancellation or billing detail nearby.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source covers subscription facts directly, general practice

steps: List plan terms, cancellation policy and billing cadence from the brand record.
Add them as a fact block next to the price on the subscription PDP.
Publish the same terms on the facts page.
Test how do I cancel [brand] on an AI engine and confirm it returns the site's own policy.

test.method: Run a cancellation-policy prompt against the brand and check the answer.

title: Treat marketplace listings as a citation surface, not only a sales channel
hypothesis: If Amazon and other marketplace listing titles, bullets, price and rating stay consistent with the PDP, then an engine that reads the marketplace page states the same facts as the brand's own site.

signal.check: Marketplace revenue sits alongside the owned site with no check on whether listings match the PDP.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source measures whether engines cite marketplace listings

steps: Compare listing title, bullets, price and rating against the PDP for top marketplace SKUs.
Fix any mismatch.
Check whether cited domains in the prompt audit include the marketplace.
Recheck quarterly as listings and prices drift.

test.method: Check the prompt audit's cited domains list for marketplace URLs.

title: Build the buyer question list from the catalog first, then mine keywords
hypothesis: If the question list starts from the catalog's fit, sizing, compatibility and use-case attributes before any keyword tool runs, then the resulting pages match real chat queries better because keyword tools do not hold long conversational chat phrasing.

signal.check: Content or test-set work is starting with a keyword tool export instead of a catalog-based question list.

expected_effect.size: unknown; direction only

steps: List the catalog's fit, sizing, compatibility and use-case attributes.
Turn each attribute into a real question a buyer might ask.
Tag each question with the SKU or collection it belongs to.
Only then run a keyword tool to fill remaining gaps.

test.method: Check every question is tagged with a SKU or collection.
test.read_point: At the start of any content or test-set work

title: Mine People Also Ask at depth for buyer questions
hypothesis: If People Also Ask is expanded at depth for each core term, then a large pool of real buyer questions surfaces because one demo returned 143 questions from a single term at depth 3.

signal.check: A research run is starting and People Also Ask has not been expanded past the first visible layer.

expected_effect.size: one demo at depth 3 returned 143 questions from a single term

risk.note: Research task only; results still need manual trimming.

steps: Search each core term and expand People Also Ask boxes repeatedly.
Keep expanding nested questions to at least depth 3.
Export the full list.
Trim by hand, keeping only questions a real buyer would ask about products the brand sells.

test.method: Count kept questions after trimming versus the raw export.

title: Pull tail questions from support tickets, sales calls and live chat
hypothesis: If real buyer questions get pulled from support tickets, sales calls and live chat, then the content plan covers tail questions with no search volume that a keyword tool would never surface.

signal.check: A research run relies only on keyword tools and People Also Ask, with no pull from support or sales data.

expected_effect.size: unknown; these questions carry no search volume by definition, so size is not measurable this way

prerequisites: Access to support tickets, sales notes and chat logs
steps: Pull a sample of support tickets, sales call notes and live chat logs.
Extract recurring buyer questions with no obvious search-tool equivalent.
Tag each with the SKU or collection it targets.
Add them to the master question list.

test.method: Check how many tail questions convert into published FAQ or guide content.

title: Mine Reddit threads in your category for buyer questions
hypothesis: If category-relevant Reddit threads get read for the real questions buyers ask each other, then the question list covers phrasing and concerns a keyword tool misses entirely.

signal.check: A research run has not checked Reddit threads in the category for recurring buyer questions.

expected_effect.size: unknown; source recommendation only

risk.note: Research only; no posting involved here.

steps: Search Reddit for the category's main terms.
Read the top threads and note recurring buyer questions and concerns.
Extract phrasing that differs from typical keyword-tool terms.
Add the extracted questions to the master list, tagged by SKU or collection.

test.method: Compare Reddit-sourced questions against the existing keyword-based list for overlap and gaps.

title: Never turn AI fan-out sub-queries into a keyword or page list
hypothesis: If fan-out sub-queries are used only to check topic coverage and borrow phrasing, and never turned into a keyword list or a page per phrase, then content effort is not wasted, because over 95% of fan-out sub-queries have zero search volume and change run to run.

signal.check: A tool exports fan-out phrases and someone proposes building a page per phrase.

expected_effect.size: over 95% of fan-out sub-queries reported to have zero search volume

risk.note: A decision rule; prevents wasted content effort.

steps: When fan-out phrases are exported, use them only to check coverage on an existing page.
Borrow useful phrasing for headings and titles.
Reject any proposal to build a new URL for a fan-out phrase alone.
Log the fan-out count seen for the brand's own prompts instead of assuming a fixed number.

test.method: Check the content plan for any URL created only because of a fan-out phrase.

title: Route transactional questions to PDP pages, informational ones to guides
hypothesis: If transactional questions route to PDP and collection pages while informational ones route to guides and FAQs, then each page keeps its focus and each question gets the right kind of answer.

signal.check: A research export lists questions with no page-type assignment.

expected_effect.size: unknown; direction only

steps: Review each question and classify it transactional or informational.
Route transactional questions to the relevant PDP or collection as a short FAQ item.
Route full informational topics to a guide.
Confirm every research row carries a page type and target URL.

test.method: Audit the research export for rows missing a page type.

title: Check whether the AI Overview already answers a keyword before writing for it
hypothesis: If every keyword gets a BID score and a live AI Overview read before content hours are booked, then writing effort skips terms the Overview already fully answers, saving hours for terms that can still earn a click or a mention.

signal.check: Content budget is about to be booked for a keyword with no BID score or live-answer check done.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is an efficiency filter, not a direct traffic lever

steps: Score the keyword on Business potential, Intent match and Difficulty (BID).
Search the term and read the AI Overview as a shopper would.
If the Overview fully answers it, drop it as a click target and retarget it as a mention play, a tool query, or a transactional term instead.
Record the BID score and the AI-filter verdict per row.

test.method: Track which booked keywords produced clicks versus which the Overview had already absorbed.
test.read_point: Before booking content hours, then 8 weeks after

title: Ask the target prompt on 2 to 3 AI platforms before writing the page
hypothesis: If every brief starts with the target prompt run on 2 to 3 AI platforms, then the writer knows which page types and domains already win, and prioritizes a mention on a dominant domain over trying to out-rank it.

signal.check: A content brief is being written with no note of which page types and domains currently win the target prompt.

expected_effect.size: unknown; direction only

steps: Run the target prompt on 2 to 3 priority AI platforms.
Note whether cited pages are listicles, collection pages, articles or videos.
Note which domains recur across the answers.
If a big retailer or review site is consistently cited, prioritize a mention there over trying to out-rank it.

test.method: Record the winning format and recurring domains in the brief before writing.

title: Ask each AI engine what it looks for when recommending your category
hypothesis: If each engine is asked what it looks for when recommending the category, then PDP and listing copy can be tested against a real criteria list, adding only true facts that match it.

signal.check: A PDP or listing audit is starting with no criteria list to test copy against.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim

risk.note: Never invent a certification or claim just to satisfy the list; add only verifiable facts.

steps: Ask several engines what do you look for when recommending [category].
Merge the answers into a single criteria checklist.
Mark each criterion present, absent or not true for the brand.
Add only accurate, verifiable facts that match the list to product copy and listings.

test.method: Recheck the criteria checklist against updated copy after changes.
test.read_point: After the audit and copy update

title: Keep one AI workspace holding the brand brief and every research export
hypothesis: If a single AI project or workspace holds the brand brief, catalog, keyword exports and competitor sitemaps, then drafting stays consistent because a single chat forgets earlier detail once content work runs past a week.

signal.check: Content work is running past 1 week with no persistent workspace holding the brief and research exports.

expected_effect.size: unknown; workflow efficiency claim only

steps: Create a project or persistent workspace in the AI tool being used.
Add the brand brief covering catalog, categories, target buyer and fulfilment areas.
Add every keyword export and competitor sitemap as it is produced.
Check the workspace's brief matches the brand record's current fact sheet.

test.method: Spot-check that the workspace brief matches the current fact sheet.
test.read_point: Monthly, or whenever the fact sheet changes

title: Aim outreach at review sites and gift guides first, then forums, then owned channels
hypothesis: If tier-1 outreach targets editorial review sites and gift-guide listicles before tier-2 forums and tier-3 owned channels, then mention effort lands on the hardest, most valuable placements first while they still have runway before a season or launch.

signal.check: The mention gap is the biggest gap from the audit, and no tiered outreach plan exists yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown; sequencing recommendation, no measured figure

prerequisites: Gap analysis showing mentions as the biggest gap
steps: Build the mention target list with 3 tiers: editorial/review, community, owned.
Prioritize tier-1 review sites and seasonal gift guides first.
Move to tier-2 forums once tier-1 outreach is underway.
Keep tier-3 owned channels (YouTube, podcast, LinkedIn) positive and on topic in parallel.

test.method: Track placements landed per tier and whether each then appears in the prompt audit's citations.

title: Get onto the third-party listicles engines already cite for your category
hypothesis: If outreach targets the specific listicles an AI engine already cites for the category, instead of publishing new ones, then the store earns a mention on a source engines already trust.

signal.check: The mention target list is being built with no check of which listicles the engine already cites for best [category].

expected_effect.size: unknown; direction only

steps: Run best [category] on AI Overviews and AI Mode and open every cited listicle.
Use a content search for title:best or title:versus plus category terms, minus the brand name.
Skip listicles owned by direct competitors.
Pitch each target with a specific, credible case for inclusion, tracked in a sheet.

test.method: Track placements won per month and whether each then appears in the citation check.

title: Only pay for a placement the publisher labels sponsored or affiliate
hypothesis: If a paid placement only goes ahead when the publisher labels it sponsored or affiliate, then the brand stays compliant and avoids the reputational and legal risk of presenting paid coverage as editorial.

signal.check: A publisher quotes a price for inclusion, or a vendor proposes a paid placement.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a compliance gate, not a growth lever

risk.note: Skipping this check risks disclosure violations and platform penalties.

prerequisites: Legal review of any paid placement
steps: When a publisher quotes a price, confirm they will label the placement sponsored or affiliate.
Route the deal through legal and budget review before paying.
Reject any placement presented as independent editorial or an industry report.
Record the disclosure label per placement in the mention target list.

test.method: Audit every paid placement for a visible disclosure label.
test.read_point: At every paid placement, and quarterly overall

title: Answer in Reddit threads engines already cite, as one named employee
hypothesis: If a real, named employee posts 1 genuinely useful answer in a thread an engine already cites for the target question, then the brand earns a citation-worthy mention because fake accounts and spam get detected and deleted.

signal.check: A category thread already appears in an AI answer and the brand has not participated in it.

expected_effect.size: one case saw a new Reddit post cited on ChatGPT within about 30 to 45 days, next day on Perplexity

risk.note: A moderator can delete a comment at any time; never fight it, and never use fake accounts.

prerequisites: A real employee willing to post under their name and employer
steps: From the prompt set, list Reddit threads that already appear in answers for priority prompts.
Check thread age, whether it is locked, and the subreddit's self-promotion rules.
Post 1 useful, on-topic answer from a named account stating the employer, no pitch.
Lead with an open-ecosystem angle rather than we are better than X.
Watch the thread for negative comments and respond early and honestly.

test.method: Log any citation of the thread in the spreadsheet after posting.

title: Budget Reddit mainly for ChatGPT, expect a month lag
hypothesis: If Reddit effort is budgeted mainly against ChatGPT with a 1 to 2 month lag expected, then the founder judges the program fairly because Reddit's influence concentrates almost entirely there and only a few slots exist per answer.

signal.check: Reddit effort is being sized against listicles and video without checking which platforms actually cite Reddit for this brand's prompts.

expected_effect.size: one case reported a 30 to 45 day lag to citation on ChatGPT and only about 4 to 5 Reddit references per answer

steps: Check the prompt set's cited domains to see which platforms cite Reddit for the brand's own prompts.
Size Reddit budget mainly against ChatGPT visibility.
Set expectations for a 1 to 2 month lag before a comment shows up in citations.
Never rely on Reddit as the only mention channel; a platform can drop Reddit citations for a period.

test.method: Track which platforms cite Reddit for the brand's prompts before and after the program runs.

title: Make or commission a search-hit YouTube video for a cited category term
hypothesis: If the store makes or commissions a video for a term that already ranks in YouTube search, with the keyword spoken aloud and in the title, then it earns AI citations because YouTube is one of the most cited domains in AI answers.

signal.check: The format gap shows video cited for the category and the store has none.

expected_effect.size: one vendor study puts YouTube at 5.6% of AI Overview citations and a 0.737 correlation with ChatGPT visibility

risk.note: Disclose any sponsored creator video on screen and in the description.

prerequisites: Ability to make or commission video
steps: Find topics where a YouTube watch URL already ranks top 3 for a niche term.
Choose the video format that already ranks: tutorial, review, best-of.
Put the exact keyword in the title, the first 2 lines of the description, and speak it in the first and last 10 seconds.
Publish a companion blog page and link both ways.
Add the video's target prompts to the test set.

test.method: Check whether the video URL appears in prompt citations within a quarter.

title: Ask every buyer for an honest review, never pay, script or filter it
hypothesis: If every buyer gets a neutral post-purchase review request on the platforms engines already cite for the category, then honest review volume grows because engines draw on review platforms unprompted and repeat what they find.

signal.check: The prompt audit shows a review platform driving a negative or wrong answer, or review volume is low on the platforms engines cite.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no measured lift given, source recommendation only

risk.note: Never incentivise, script or condition the request; several review platforms prohibit incentives.

prerequisites: Post-purchase survey or review request flow
steps: Choose review platforms from the prompt audit's cited domains and from where buyers already post.
Send a neutral post-purchase request about fit, quality and limitations, in the customer's own words.
Never script outcomes, offer an incentive or send only to happy buyers.
Spread requests across multiple platforms rather than relying on one.

test.method: Track review count and rating per cited platform monthly.

title: Send a press release only for real news, with the target phrase up top
hypothesis: If a press release covers only a real launch, award or sponsorship with the target phrase in the title, subhead and first line, then it can get the store cited for that phrase, because one cheap release did exactly this in a tracked case.

signal.check: A real launch, award won or sponsorship has happened with no press release planned.

expected_effect.size: one tracked case used an about $80 wire release and got the target phrase cited

risk.note: Never fabricate news or claims; a fabricated release is prohibited and reputationally risky.

steps: Confirm the news is real: launch, award actually won, sponsorship, or original research with a described method.
Put the exact target phrase in the title, subheading and first sentence.
If reporting research, state method, sample, dates and who paid; never title a promotional ranking an industry report.
Distribute via a wire service and record cost and syndication outlets.
Re-run the relevant prompts after 4 weeks.

test.method: Rerun the target prompt 4 weeks after distribution.

title: Put your founder or product expert on reporter platforms and podcasts
hypothesis: If the founder or a product expert answers reporter-request pitches and appears on category podcasts, then the brand earns citable third-party mentions because transcripts get indexed and articles carry the expert's authority.
does_not_apply_when: No founder or in-house expert is available to speak with authority on the category

signal.check: The brand has a founder or expert who can speak with authority on materials, sourcing or fit, and is not yet pitching reporter platforms or podcasts.

expected_effect.size: one source reports a 5 of 12 pitched-to-published hit rate on a free tier, as an example not a target

steps: Create an account on a current reporter-request platform.
Answer only the pitches that genuinely fit the brand's expertise.
Pitch category podcasts and industry publications already cited in the category.
Structure any resulting long-form piece like site content: answer first, then a TL;DR and tables.

test.method: Log each published piece with the outlet's citation status.

title: Keep name, price and facts identical across site, feed and every marketplace listing
hypothesis: If name, price and product facts stay character-identical across the site, Shopping feed and every marketplace listing, then engines reading any of those sources repeat the same correct facts.

signal.check: No listings sheet exists tracking last-verified date per platform, before any paid mention work starts.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no numeric figure given

steps: List every platform carrying the brand's name, price or product facts.
Compare each against the fact sheet and the site.
Fix any mismatch found.
If managing more than about 3 listings, use a reputable citation service rather than a bulk cheap seller.

test.method: Keep a listings sheet with a last-verified date per platform.
test.read_point: Before any paid mention work, and after any price or policy change

title: Chase backlinks last, judge by relevance, and never buy them
hypothesis: If backlink outreach comes only after content, indexing and mentions are already working, and every publisher is judged for relevance and real readers, then link risk stays low because paid links carry manual-action risk with search engines.

signal.check: The store still trails competitors after content and indexing work is done, and a link-buying proposal is on the table.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no measured figure, direction only

risk.note: Buying links risks a manual action penalty; never do it despite it being common practice in some circles.

prerequisites: Content published, indexing confirmed, and still not competitive
steps: Confirm content, indexing and mention work is already done before considering links.
Judge each potential publisher's relevance and real audience on a call.
Never pay for a link or a bulk citation service.
Report link work separately from the AEO program.

test.method: Track organic ranking movement after any earned link.
test.read_point: 8 to 12 weeks after any earned placement

title: Add LinkedIn, Medium or Quora only if they already show up in AI answers
