hypothesis: If a secondary platform like LinkedIn, Medium or Quora only gets budget once it already shows up in the brand's own cited-domains list, then effort is not wasted on a platform with thin or unpredictable AI citation.

signal.check: Tier-1 and tier-2 work (listicles and Reddit) is already running and a plan proposes adding a secondary platform.

expected_effect.size: unknown; one source calls LinkedIn citation thin and unpredictable

prerequisites: Tier-1 and tier-2 mention work already running
steps: Check the prompt set's cited-domains list for any secondary platform appearing.
Only add budget to a platform that already shows up there or that buyers clearly use.
Structure any long-form piece on that platform like site content.
Recheck which platforms are indexed and cited each quarter.

test.method: Track whether the added platform starts appearing in citations.

title: Correct a wrong AI fact at the site first, then the publisher, then everywhere
hypothesis: If a wrong AI fact gets corrected on the site first, then at the third-party publisher, then distributed across every channel, then the correction spreads through the sources engines actually read, even though it moves slowly.

signal.check: The prompt audit shows a wrong price, spec or policy in an AI answer.

expected_effect.size: unknown; one tracked case of a memory-based correction took about 2 years to move partway

steps: Publish the correct, specific fact on the site first.
Request a correction from the third-party publisher.
Distribute the corrected claim through third-party articles, founder video and press if it persists.
Re-run the fixed question set monthly, logging model, date and cited evidence, until the answer holds twice.

test.method: Re-run the audit row monthly until the answer holds twice.

title: Loop the affiliate manager into the AI mention plan
hypothesis: If the affiliate manager joins the mention planning, then tier-1 review publisher relationships get pursued faster because durable, high-authority publishers usually work through affiliate programs.
does_not_apply_when: The brand runs no affiliate program

signal.check: The brand runs an affiliate program and the mention target list was built without the affiliate manager's input.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim

prerequisites: An affiliate program or affiliate budget
steps: Identify durable, high-authority publishers in the category that run affiliate programs.
Bring the affiliate manager into the mention target list review.
Mark which mention targets run an affiliate program.
Run a link-intersection analysis on competitors to see which listicles and guest posts they appear in.

test.method: Track affiliate-program placements landed after coordination.

title: Run a 6-gap AI visibility audit on your store and named competitors
hypothesis: If the store and each named competitor get audited for visibility, narrative, topic, format, mention and demand gaps, then the AEO plan targets the real gaps instead of guessing, because each gap type needs a different fix.

signal.check: It is the start of an engagement or a quarter, and no gap sheet exists.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this produces a prioritized fix list, not a direct metric move

steps: Classify each finding into visibility, narrative, topic, format, mentions or demand.
Label each finding fix, build or influence.
Repeat the identical audit on named competitors, including marketplace listings.
Score findings by demand, credibility and citation odds, and pick quick wins first.

test.method: Review the gap sheet for completeness: every row has a gap type, a fix label and a source.

title: List every brand entity before you audit AI visibility
hypothesis: If the brand, sub-brands, hero SKU names, proprietary materials and founder names are listed before the audit runs, then each entity gets its own visibility profile instead of being missed.

signal.check: A gap audit is about to run with no entity list prepared.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a precondition step, not a direct metric mover

steps: List the brand, sub-brands, hero SKU names, proprietary materials and founder names.
Attach the categories and attributes each entity should be associated with.
Use adjectives and modifiers buyers already use for each.
Confirm every audit prompt names 1 entity from this list.

test.method: Check every audit prompt references an entity from the list.

title: Ask each AI engine what it knows about your brand, then open every source
hypothesis: If every priority platform gets asked to search the internet and tell me what you know about the brand, and every cited source gets opened, then the real drivers of the brand's AI description become visible instead of assumed.

signal.check: It has been a month or more since the last brand-knowledge audit, or a PR event, launch or complaint just happened.

expected_effect.size: unknown; an audit step, not a direct metric mover

steps: Prompt each priority platform: search the internet and tell me what you know about [brand].
Read the answer as a shopper would.
Open every citation to see which pages shape the answer.
Repeat the same prompt for each competitor to find sources driving their recommendations.

test.method: Log cited sources with date and platform each run.
test.read_point: Monthly, and after any PR event, launch or complaint

title: Check whether an AI answer came from live search or memory before acting on it
hypothesis: If each audit row records whether the answer came from a live search or from memory, then the fix targets the right lever, because a memory-based answer needs third-party source fixes rather than a site edit.

signal.check: An audit answer shows no citations or wildly inconsistent citations across repeated runs.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a diagnostic step, not a direct metric mover

steps: Run the identical prompt in an incognito or logged-out session and in a logged-in session.
Repeat a few times with varied wording.
If citations are missing or wildly inconsistent, mark the answer as memory-based.
Note whether the answer shows a shoppable card or format that implies live retrieval.

test.method: Log mode, citations and format for each audit row.

title: Filter your AI tracker for mentioned-but-not-cited and others-only gaps
hypothesis: If a tracker or manual prompt log gets filtered for mentioned-but-not-cited, others-only, and topic-ownership views, then the mention short list writes itself because these filters point straight at missed citations and competitor-only slots.

signal.check: A tracker is in place, or a manual prompt log exists, with no gap filtering applied yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a filtering method, not a direct metric mover

prerequisites: A tracker or a manual prompt log
steps: Filter for brand named but PDP not linked (a missed citation).
Filter for competitors named and the brand absent (others only).
Filter for which brand the engine associates with each topic.
Feed the others-only list, filtered for best, top, versus and alternative terms, into the mention target list within the week.

test.method: Check the mention target list is refreshed weekly from these filters.

title: Fix the single biggest AI visibility gap first, take the quick wins
hypothesis: If the plan names 1 gap and 1 fix for the month instead of trying to close every gap at once, then real progress shows up faster because a spread-thin plan rarely finishes anything.

signal.check: A gap analysis just finished and the plan lists many gaps with no single priority.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a prioritisation method, not a direct metric mover

steps: Rank gaps by demand, credibility and citation odds.
Pick the single biggest gap and a named quick win for the month.
Do not start a second gap's fix until the first shows a result.
Repeat after every gap analysis.

test.method: Check the plan names exactly 1 gap and 1 fix for the month.

title: Repeat the AI visibility audit monthly, with a deeper pass every quarter
hypothesis: If share of voice, cited domains, category coverage and sentiment get checked monthly and a deep competitive audit runs quarterly, then drift gets caught early because GEO is an ongoing program, not a one-time project.

signal.check: A baseline exists but no recurring monthly or quarterly audit is scheduled.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a cadence fix, not a direct metric mover

steps: Schedule a monthly check of share of voice, cited domains, category coverage and sentiment.
Schedule a deeper competitive audit each quarter.
Put both dates on the AEO calendar.
Report all 4 monthly lines plus the quarter's audit date in the report.

test.method: Confirm the monthly report carries all 4 lines and the quarter's audit date.

title: Split AI-referred sessions by page type and customer status before judging them
hypothesis: If AI-referred sessions get split by landing page type and new versus returning customer, then the channel gets judged correctly, because a guide with no orders needs different action than a PDP with few clicks but real orders.

signal.check: The GA4 AI channel has a month of data and the report treats it as one undifferentiated number.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source splits AI referrals this way yet, general practice

prerequisites: GA4 AI channel with at least 1 month of data
steps: Pull AI-referred sessions split by landing page type: PDP, collection, guide.
Split again by new versus returning customer.
Add the split to the monthly report.
Route each finding to the matching fix: links for a guide, more citations for a PDP.

test.method: Check the monthly report carries the split for any store with more than a handful of AI-referred sessions.

title: Measure AI visibility with 3 pillars together: referrals, bot logs and survey
hypothesis: If AI referral sessions, bot visits and the checkout survey all run together from week 1, then AI visibility gets measured completely, because no single pillar catches zero-click influence, live reads and actual behaviour at once.

signal.check: AEO content work is starting or already running with fewer than all 3 measurement pillars live.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a completeness fix, not a direct metric mover

prerequisites: Server logs or a bot-analytics tool
steps: Set up the GA4 AI referral channel.
Set up bot logging or a bot-analytics tool for citation bot visits.
Add the how did you hear about us survey question at checkout.
Run all 3 together before or alongside any content work, so day 1 is measured.

test.method: Confirm all 3 pillars return data within 2 weeks.
test.read_point: Within 2 weeks of setup, then monthly

title: Build a GA4 channel that tracks AI-referred sessions
hypothesis: If a dedicated GA4 channel group matches AI referrer hostnames, then AI-referred sessions become visible and countable as a floor, because several platforms strip referrers and undercount the real number.

signal.check: No GA4 channel group separates AI referrers from generic Referral traffic.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this reveals existing traffic rather than creating new traffic; treat the count as a floor

risk.note: Channel group changes are non-destructive; remove the channel if it mis-buckets traffic.

steps: In GA4 Admin, Data Display, Channel Groups, copy the default group.
Add a channel matching current AI referrer hostnames by regex.
Place the new channel above Referral in the channel order.
Verify sessions show up correctly in Traffic Acquisition.

test.method: Check the channel shows sessions, add-to-cart and orders.

title: Ask how did you hear about us with AI options listed first
hypothesis: If the checkout survey lists AI assistant options up front instead of under Other, then self-reported AI attribution rises because burying the option under Other suppresses honest answers.

signal.check: The checkout or post-purchase survey either has no AI options or buries them under Other.

expected_effect.size: one company reported a sharp rise in self-reported AI mentions after moving the options out of Other

steps: Add AI assistant, and named platforms like ChatGPT and Perplexity, as visible options.
List them above generic channels like Other.
Keep a free-text field for anything not listed.
Compare the survey's AI share against the GA4 AI channel share each month.

test.method: Compare survey AI share before and after the reorder.

title: Track which pages AI citation bots actually fetch
hypothesis: If server logs or a bot-analytics tool track citation-bot visits separately from training-bot visits, then the store learns which pages are actually used as sources, because repeated citation-bot visits signal real use in answers.

signal.check: Server logs or bot-analytics data are available but not yet split into citation bots versus training bots.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a visibility fix, not a direct metric mover

prerequisites: Server log access or a bot-analytics integration
steps: Enable server log access or a bot-analytics integration with citation-bot tagging.
Separate citation bots from training bots in the reporting.
List the top 20 pages fetched by citation bots each month.
If no bot visits appear on key pages, check internal links and access rules before assuming a crawl problem.

test.method: Review the monthly top-20 fetched-page list.

title: Report AI share of voice on a frozen prompt set, run several times
hypothesis: If a set of 100 to 200 buyer questions stays frozen and runs 3 or more times per platform on a schedule, then share of voice becomes a real, comparable number instead of noise, because answers are probabilistic and vary run to run.

signal.check: No frozen, versioned prompt set exists, or prompts change between reporting periods.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a measurement setup, not a direct growth lever

steps: Select 100 to 200 questions across intents and freeze the list.
Run every question 3 or more times per priority platform.
Record date, model, mode, named, cited, competitors and cited URLs for each run.
Let it run 2 weeks before any intervention to see baseline variance.
Compute share of voice in code, not in the model.

test.method: Confirm every row has 3 or more runs per platform.

title: Prove one AEO tactic with a control group before calling it a rule
hypothesis: If a prompt set splits into a test group and an untouched control group before applying 1 tactic, then a claimed AEO win becomes credible, because most AEO best practices have never been tested this way.

signal.check: A tactic is about to be called proven for this store with no test-versus-control comparison run.

expected_effect.size: one source's design uses 200 questions split 100 test and 100 control, run about 2 weeks

risk.note: If a page change causes the test group to fall while control holds, revert from the saved copy.

prerequisites: Frozen prompt set baseline already running
steps: Split the prompt set into a matched test and control group.
Leave the control group untouched for the whole test.
Apply exactly 1 tactic to the test group only.
Wait about 2 weeks, then compare the change in test against the change in control.
Only adopt the tactic as a rule after a second run replicates the result.

test.method: Compare the test group's share-of-voice change against control over the same window.
test.read_point: 2 weeks after applying the tactic, replicated once more before adoption

title: Never accept a raw AI citation or mention count as a win
hypothesis: If a report is checked for which prompts, whether search fired, mention versus citation, and whether orders moved before a citation count is believed, then vanity metrics stop passing as results, because 1 URL can be cited across endless phrasing variants.

signal.check: A vendor report or internal report shows a raw citation or mention count as the headline number.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a reporting discipline fix, not a growth lever

steps: When a report shows a citation count, ask which prompts produced it.
Ask whether a live search actually fired for those prompts.
Ask whether it was a mention or a linked citation.
Ask whether orders moved; reject the count as a headline if any answer is missing.

test.method: Check every vendor report and internal report answers all 4 questions.

title: Read Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools monthly for AI-cited pages
lever: GSC and Bing AI performance review
hypothesis: If Search Console impressions and clicks and the Bing AI performance tab get read monthly, then real direction shows up even as click-through falls, because impressions usually rise before clicks as answers absorb queries.

signal.check: No monthly read of Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools exists for the money pages.

expected_effect.size: one vendor reports a 58% CTR drop on the number 1 organic result under an AI Overview as of December 2025

prerequisites: Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools access
steps: Pull clicks, impressions and average position for the money pages in Search Console.
Pull total citations, average pages cited and cited queries from Bing's AI performance tab.
Split the read by page type: PDP, collection, guide.
Judge direction month over month; do not promise a fixed growth target.

test.method: Track the page-type split month over month.

title: Compare AI-referred conversion rate, AOV and revenue against organic every month
hypothesis: If AI-referred order conversion rate, AOV and revenue per session sit side by side with organic every month, then the real question, whether the traffic produced more revenue, gets answered instead of a chart that just looks good.

signal.check: The monthly report shows AI channel traffic with no side-by-side comparison against organic conversion and revenue.

expected_effect.size: unknown; direction only, comparison method

steps: Pull AI-referred conversion rate, AOV and revenue per session.
Pull the same 3 metrics for organic traffic over the same window.
Show both side by side with session counts visible.
Ask whether the traffic produced more revenue, not just a bigger chart.

test.method: Review the side-by-side comparison every month.

title: Log every AI citation found and recheck it for persistence
hypothesis: If every citation found gets logged with query, platform, date, URL and page type, and the same queries get rechecked, then citation persistence becomes visible even without a paid tracker.

signal.check: No citation log exists, whether or not a paid tracker is in use.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a logging discipline, not a direct metric mover

steps: Start a spreadsheet with columns: query, platform, date, URL, named, cited.
Log every citation found during audits and prompt runs.
Recheck the same queries on a schedule.
Show how many months each URL has held its citation.

test.method: Review months-held per cited URL.

title: Track about 3 AI platforms and buy the cheapest tracker that does the job
hypothesis: If tracking stays to about 3 priority platforms and the cheapest tool that covers them gets chosen, then measurement cost stays proportionate, because most trackers are functionally commodity keyword trackers sold at wildly different prices.

signal.check: A tracker purchase is being considered with no comparison against 2 cheaper options.

expected_effect.size: unknown; roughly 60 comparable trackers exist by one estimate

risk.note: Purchase decision only; check the budget ledger first.

steps: List the surfaces tracked, prompt limits, run frequency, logged-in support and export format for candidate tools.
Compare pricing against at least 2 cheaper options.
Confirm the tool cost sits within the budget ledger before purchase.
Pick the cheapest tool that covers about 3 priority surfaces.

test.method: Compare the chosen tool's price against the 2 cheaper alternatives reviewed.

title: Ask a GEO vendor 5 questions and 3 probes before hiring them
hypothesis: If a GEO vendor answers 5 core questions and 3 probe questions on a call before signing, then a weak or gray-hat vendor gets caught early, because vague answers and grifter probes are reliable warning signs.

signal.check: Any agency or tool purchase is being considered for AEO work.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a vetting method, not a direct metric mover

steps: Ask how GEO differs from SEO, and how long they have operated in optimisation.
Ask for recent case studies and how those clients perform today, not just at launch.
Ask their stance on off-site work, and whether they publish hundreds of blog posts.
Probe with llms.txt, an AI info page, and chunking everything; an enthusiastic yes is a caution sign.
Ask for a store case with order conversion and AOV, not sign-ups.

test.method: Record answers verbatim on the vendor vetting sheet.

title: Audit a vendor case study by keyword difficulty band, and ask how it looks now
hypothesis: If a vendor's case-study keywords get split at a difficulty threshold and checked band by band, then a rank-and-tank pattern gets caught before signing, because a rising total can hide declining hard-category terms.

signal.check: A vendor case study lands on the desk showing a blended traffic chart with no difficulty split.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a validity check, not a direct metric mover

steps: Split the case study's keywords at a difficulty threshold, such as above 30.
Chart trends for each band separately.
Check whether category and collection terms decline under a rising total.
Verify the claimed results in your own tool instead of trusting a screenshot.

test.method: Compare 2 trend lines per case study instead of 1 blended line.

title: Treat every AEO statistic in a vendor pitch as a snapshot, not a fact
hypothesis: If every AEO statistic used in a client report gets attributed to its source and never presented as an industry fact, then the founder makes decisions on honest evidence instead of an interested party's unlinked study.

signal.check: A big number is about to go into a client report or a plan with no source attribution.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a hygiene fix, not a growth lever

steps: Before quoting a number, find its original source and whether the study is published.
Attribute the number to that source in the report.
Never present a vendor-only or unsourced number as a fact.
Use direction, not the precise figure, when the source is a vendor's own unpublished study.

test.method: Check every number in a report carries its source.

title: Do not publish your own best of lists that hide competitors
hypothesis: If the brand never self-publishes best of lists on Medium, Substack, LinkedIn or Quora that put itself first and hide competitors, then it avoids a tactic assistants already route around, because engines already search review sites when a listicle looks self-serving.

signal.check: A vendor or team member proposes publishing the brand's own best of category list that omits competitors.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a policy gate, not a growth lever

risk.note: Reject the tactic outright rather than trying a softened version.

steps: When a self-published best of list is proposed, reject it outright.
Explain that assistants already route around self-serving listicles.
Redirect the effort to earning placement on listicles engines already trust.
Search Medium, Substack, LinkedIn and Quora periodically for any existing self-published list that hides competitors, and remove it.

test.method: Search these platforms for the brand's own best of lists.

title: Never invent a certification, award or number to satisfy an AI checklist
hypothesis: If every claim, certification and number traces back to the verified brand record before publishing, then the brand avoids a fabricated fact spreading through AI answers the way a planted false claim can.

signal.check: A criteria list from an AI recommendation audit shows a gap, and someone proposes adding a certification or number the brand does not actually hold.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a compliance gate, not a growth lever

risk.note: A fabricated claim can spread through AI answers and third-party sites and is very hard to fully retract.

steps: Check every proposed claim, certification, award or rating against the brand record.
Reject any claim the brand cannot verify, no matter what an AI criteria list asks for.
If a real gap exists, close it with a real fact or a real certification process, not a claim.
Add the claim only once it is verified and in the fact sheet.

test.method: Audit any new claim against the brand record before publishing.

title: Do not treat an unproven AEO tactic as settled fact
hypothesis: If off-site and format tactics stay labelled as hypotheses until a control-group test replicates a result, then the AEO plan is not oversold, because sources disagree on whether tactics beyond quality content and crawlability actually work.

signal.check: A plan or a vendor pitch presents Reddit, video or mention tactics as proven without a replicated test.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a discipline fix, not a growth lever

risk.note: A framing discipline; prevents overselling to the founder.

steps: Run the common-ground work first: crawler access, measurement, and answer-first content.
Label every off-site or format tactic a hypothesis until tested.
Only call a tactic proven for this store after a control-group test replicates the result.
Never sell a tactic to the founder as established before that replication happens.

test.method: Check every claimed win traces to a replicated control-group test.
test.read_point: Before presenting any tactic as proven

title: Run a full technical crawlability audit before AEO content work starts
hypothesis: If robots.txt, Cloudflare settings, WAF rules, JS rendering, speed, headings, indexing, schema and AI-referred 404s all get checked in 1 run, then the store is confirmed retrievable before any content or mention work starts.

signal.check: AEO work is starting with no completed technical crawlability audit on file.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a foundational audit, not a direct metric mover on its own

risk.note: Read-only audit; keep a backup of robots.txt and Cloudflare settings before any edit.

prerequisites: Site URL, hosting and CDN details
steps: Check robots.txt for AI bot blocks, then set the bot access policy.
Check Cloudflare and firewall settings for the same bots.
Disable JavaScript and confirm content shows on 4 key pages.
Run Lighthouse and check heading hierarchy on the same 4 pages.
Confirm indexing in Search Console and Bing, and check for AI-referred 404s.
Validate schema on the 4 pages and write the crawlability fix list with owner and priority.

test.method: Re-fetch robots.txt and re-run the checklist after every CDN, theme, app or platform change.
test.read_point: Before content work starts, and after every platform change

title: Write and deploy a documented AI-bot access policy
hypothesis: If the brand writes down its search-bot-versus-training-bot decision and deploys it as a robots.txt policy, then future theme, app or CDN changes cannot silently undo it, because the policy exists as a reference document, not tribal knowledge.

signal.check: The store has decided on a bot policy verbally or ad hoc, with nothing written down to check future changes against.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a documentation fix, not a direct metric mover

risk.note: Keep the previous robots.txt as a backup.

steps: List each vendor's search bot and training bot by current name.
Write robots.txt rules: allow search bots, apply the brand's training-bot choice, keep private paths blocked.
Prefer a platform or CDN toggle over raw edits if one exists that separates indexing from training.
Deploy, re-fetch robots.txt, and re-run the bot-access checker.

test.method: Re-fetch robots.txt after deployment and recheck quarterly.

title: Run the full brand and competitor AI visibility gap analysis
hypothesis: If the entity list, SEO baseline, tracker filters, gap classification and a 4-part SEO competitor pass all run together, then the resulting gap list points to the single highest-value fix instead of a scattered set of observations.

signal.check: It is the start of an engagement or a quarter and no complete gap list (D6) exists yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this produces a prioritized list rather than a direct metric move

steps: Write the entity list and record the SEO baseline: domain rating, referring domains, organic keywords.
Record mentions, citations and share of voice per priority platform from the tracker or 3 manual runs.
Apply the mentioned-but-not-cited, others-only and topic-association filters.
Classify every finding into 1 of 6 gaps and label it fix, build or influence.
Repeat for each named competitor, then run the 4-part SEO competitor pass.
Output the gap list and feed content rows, mention rows and format rows to the matching workflow.

test.method: Check every row of the gap list has a gap type, a fix label and a source URL or prompt.

title: Run the prompt audit and fix wrong brand facts at the source
hypothesis: If the full prompt audit runs from asking what engines know, marking each fact, opening every source, publishing the correction, and re-running monthly, then wrong brand facts get closed instead of surfacing again next quarter.

signal.check: No structured prompt audit has run for the brand yet, or wrong facts from a past audit were never tracked to closure.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles several individual fixes into 1 tracked workflow

risk.note: Corrections are additive; never delete a true but unflattering fact.

steps: On each priority platform, ask what it knows about the brand and save the answer, citations, date and model.
Repeat logged out and logged in, a few times each, to check whether search actually fired.
Mark every fact correct, wrong, missing or competitor-favouring against the fact sheet.
Open every cited source and fix what the brand controls; request correction for third-party sources.
Publish the correct facts on the site first, then repeat for each competitor as mention targets.
Re-run monthly and log changes with model and date.

test.method: Track open, closed and new wrong facts each month.

title: Run the question research pipeline from raw questions to a routed export
hypothesis: If paid terms, support tickets, People Also Ask, a keyword tool and manual trimming all feed into 1 export with intent, page type and goal per question, then every writer knows exactly what to build without repeating the research.

signal.check: Content briefs are being written without a shared, routed question export to pull from.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles several research steps into 1 usable export

steps: Pull paid-search terms and turn them into real questions with an assistant.
Add tail questions from support tickets, chat logs and Reddit threads.
Run People Also Ask at depth and seed a keyword tool with broad terms and modifiers.
Trim the combined list by hand, keeping only real buyer questions.
Run each survivor on 2 to 3 AI surfaces and apply BID plus the AI filter.
Export as a CSV with question, source, intent, page type, goal, cited domains and owner.

test.method: Confirm no row in the export lacks an intent and a page type.

title: Set up a frozen AI prompt test set and run the baseline
hypothesis: If the full 100 to 200 question set is selected, frozen, run 3 times per platform and given 2 weeks before any change, then the baseline is real and any future comparison against it is trustworthy.

signal.check: No frozen baseline exists yet, or the current prompt set changed since the last report.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a setup task producing the baseline itself

steps: Select 100 to 200 questions across intents from the research export and freeze the list.
Run every question 3 times per priority platform, in the mode buyers use.
Record date, platform, model, mode, named, cited, competitors and cited URLs for each run.
Compute share of voice and top cited domains in code.
Let the baseline run 2 weeks before any intervention.
Save the result as the visibility report's baseline.

test.method: Confirm every row has 3 runs per platform before calling it a baseline.

title: Design and run a test-vs-control AEO experiment
hypothesis: If a tactic gets tested on a matched test group against an untouched control group, and the design, dates and both curves get recorded, then the store has a real experiment record instead of a before-and-after with no comparison.

signal.check: A tactic is ready to test and no experiment design with a control group exists yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is a workflow that produces the experiment record itself

risk.note: Revert any page change from a saved copy if the test group falls while control holds.

steps: Split the prompt set into a matched test and control group.
Leave the control group untouched for the whole test.
Apply exactly 1 tactic to the test group only.
Wait about 2 weeks and re-run the baseline check on both groups.
Compare the change in test against the change in control.
Record the design, dates and both curves in the experiment record.

test.method: Only adopt the tactic as a rule after a second matched run replicates the result.
test.read_point: 2 weeks per run, replicated once before adoption

title: Rewrite one page end to end for AI citation
hypothesis: If a single page rewrite runs through intent match, phrasing, first fold, answer-first opening, atomic sections, format match, information gain, reading level and internal links in 1 pass, then the page is ready to be cited rather than partially fixed.

signal.check: A page is queued for rewrite on the catalog citation priority list.

expected_effect.size: one source's rule of thumb is about 90% of the readiness checklist ticked before calling a page ready

risk.note: Keep the previous version; revert if conversion drops.

prerequisites: Question research rows for this page
steps: Confirm intent match: transactional prompt to a buyable page, research prompt to a guide.
Set 1 primary buyer phrase for the title tag, H1 and first sentence.
Write the first fold to pass the 2-second test with a real product photo and visible CTA.
Open with a 20 to 50 word direct answer, then atomic H2 sections with named entities.
Add the winning format (table, grid, listicle), a first-hand fact, and an FAQ of 5 max.
Check reading level, internal links, meta description and schema match before publishing.

test.method: Run the page content audit checklist and confirm about 90% ticked before publishing.
test.read_point: Before publishing, then 4 to 8 weeks after

title: Build one honest comparison page against named competitors
hypothesis: If a comparison page is built with a verifiable table, honest pros and cons, legal sign-off, and a 2-month refresh plan in 1 sequence, then it stays live and defensible instead of being pulled after a challenge.
does_not_apply_when: A luxury or considered-purchase brand where naming a cheaper rival can hurt the position

signal.check: A comparison page is planned with no legal review step or refresh date attached.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles page-build steps into 1 tracked workflow

risk.note: Unpublish if a claim cannot be verified on challenge.

steps: Pick 3 to 4 competitors larger than the brand that appear in category answers.
Build the comparison table first: features, materials, price, shipping, warranty, best for.
Write pros and cons for both sides and decide deliberately who to name.
Get legal sign-off on every comparative claim for the target market.
Publish with the table near the top and an answer-first summary above it.
Refresh prices and specs every 2 months.

test.method: Recheck the comparison prompt's citations after publishing and after each refresh.
test.read_point: 4 to 8 weeks after publishing, then every 2 months

title: Refresh a sleeper page that already has links and traffic
hypothesis: If a page with real referring domains and declining traffic gets a substantive refresh, a moved date, and its prompts added to the test set in 1 pass, then citation recovery is tracked properly instead of a one-off edit nobody follows up on.

signal.check: A top-pages report shows traffic decline on a page that still has meaningful referring domains.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the refresh steps into 1 tracked workflow

risk.note: Keep the previous version before publishing the refresh.

prerequisites: Top-pages report with traffic change and referring domains
steps: Sort top pages by traffic decline and keep ones with meaningful referring domains.
Drop any page whose real problem is thin links, since a rewrite will not fix that.
Update facts, prices, specs and recommendations, and add or refresh the answer-first opening.
Move the visible last-updated date only because the content changed.
Request indexing and add the page's prompts to the test set.

test.method: Track impressions and citations within 2 months of the refresh.

title: Build the mention target list and run tier-1 outreach
hypothesis: If cited domains, competitor-driving sources and best-category listicles all feed into 1 tracked mention target list with owner, cost and disclosure fields, then outreach runs as a program instead of one-off pitches nobody tracks.

signal.check: No mention target list exists, or outreach happens ad hoc with no tracking of responses.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the outreach steps into 1 tracked workflow

risk.note: Never ask a publisher to remove competitors; skip competitor-owned pages.

prerequisites: Competitor sources from the prompt audit
Cited domains from the prompt set
steps: Collect cited domains and URLs from the prompt set and the competitor audit.
Add listicles that omit the brand, found by content search or by checking best category answers.
Remove competitor-owned pages from the list.
For each target, record owner, contact, placement type, cost, disclosure requirement and status.
Pitch with a specific, true case for inclusion, and track responses.
Re-run the prompt set 4 to 6 weeks after a placement lands.

test.method: Track responses and citation appearance per placement.
test.read_point: 4 to 6 weeks after each placement lands

title: Run a Reddit and community participation program
hypothesis: If Reddit participation runs as a program, from finding already-cited threads through karma-building to a disclosed reply, then it produces genuine citations instead of a single risky post that gets deleted.

signal.check: The store wants Reddit visibility but has no employee assigned, no subreddit list and no alert set up.

expected_effect.size: one case saw a citation appear on ChatGPT-style assistants about 30 to 45 days after a post

risk.note: A moderator can delete a post or ban an account at any time; never use fake accounts or auto-posting.

prerequisites: A real employee willing to post under their name
steps: List Reddit and forum URLs already appearing in answers for priority prompts.
Pick 5 to 10 subreddits from the buyer-persona angle and the product's problem angle, and read their rules.
Set keyword alerts for category terms.
Build karma with helpful, non-brand answers first.
When a thread fits, answer from a named account stating the employer, with 1 useful point and no pitch.
Watch cited threads for negative comments and respond early and honestly.

test.method: Log any citation of the thread after posting.

title: Produce a search-hit YouTube video and its companion page
hypothesis: If a video is built around a term that already ranks on YouTube, with keyword placement, a linked companion page and disclosed sponsorship if applicable, then the pair earns citation as a format an engine already favors for that query.

signal.check: The format gap shows video cited for the category and the store has no companion page and video pair.

expected_effect.size: unknown; individual video citation results vary widely with no clear view-count pattern

risk.note: Disclose any sponsored creator video on screen and in the description.

prerequisites: Ability to make or commission video
steps: Find a topic where a YouTube watch URL already ranks top 3 for a niche term.
Choose the video format that already ranks and keep it information-focused over polished.
Put the keyword in the title, the first lines of the description, the timestamps, and speak it aloud early and late.
Publish a companion page and link the video and page both ways.
Link the channel from the site and in Organization schema.
Add the video's target prompts to the test set.

test.method: Check whether the video URL appears in citations within a quarter.

title: Run the reviews, directories and NAP consistency workflow
hypothesis: If review collection, directory listings and NAP consistency all run as 1 coordinated workflow, then engines find the same honest facts everywhere they look instead of a patchwork of outdated listings.

signal.check: Review requests, directory listings and NAP checks are happening separately or not at all.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the program steps into 1 tracked workflow

risk.note: Never incentivise, script or condition a review request.

steps: Choose review platforms from cited domains and from where buyers already post.
Set up the neutral post-purchase review request with no incentive or condition.
Complete Google Business Profile and claim relevant directories with facts from the fact sheet.
Make NAP and key facts character-identical across every listing.
Use a reputable citation service if managing many listings; never a bulk cheap seller.
Respond to reviews and separate service fixes from any visibility effect.

test.method: Track review count, rating and listing consistency monthly.

title: Run the press release workflow for real store news
hypothesis: If a press release runs through a real-news check, phrase placement, method disclosure and a follow-up prompt re-check in 1 sequence, then it earns a citation for the target phrase without the risk of a fabricated claim.

signal.check: A real announcement, award or original research exists with no press release process attached.

expected_effect.size: one tracked case used an about $80 wire release and got the target phrase cited

risk.note: Confirm the news is real before spending on distribution; never fabricate a claim or research result.

steps: Confirm the news is real: launch, award, sponsorship or research with a described method.
Put the exact target phrase in the title, subheading and first sentence.
If reporting research, state method, sample, dates and who paid.
Distribute via a wire service and record cost and syndication outlets.
Re-run the relevant prompts after 4 weeks.

test.method: Rerun the target prompt 4 weeks after distribution.

title: Set up all 3 AI measurement pillars before content work starts
hypothesis: If the GA4 AI channel, the checkout survey, bot logs, Search Console and Bing access, and a saved conversion comparison all get built in 1 setup pass, then day 1 is measured before any content or mention work starts.

signal.check: AEO content or mention work is about to start with fewer than all 3 measurement pillars live.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the setup steps into 1 checklist

steps: Build the GA4 AI channel with current referrer hostnames and note the undercount caveat.
Add the how did you hear about us survey with AI options listed first.
Enable bot logs or a bot-analytics integration, tagging citation bots and training bots separately.
Confirm Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools access and the Bing AI performance tab.
Build a saved report comparing AI channel sessions, conversion rate and revenue against organic.
Start the citation log spreadsheet and run the prompt set baseline.

test.method: Confirm each pillar returns data within 2 weeks.

title: Build the monthly AI visibility report
hypothesis: If the monthly report pulls share of voice, mentions versus citations, prompt audit accuracy, the AI channel comparison, survey share, bot logs, GSC and Bing data, crawlability status and mention pipeline into 1 page, then the founder sees direction, not vanity numbers, every month.

signal.check: A monthly AI visibility report is due and the pieces are scattered across separate tools with no combined report.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the reporting steps into 1 tracked deliverable

steps: Re-run the prompt set and compute share of voice, citation share and top cited domains.
Report mentions and citations as separate lines, flagging named but unlinked.
Add prompt audit accuracy: wrong facts open, closed and new.
Add the GA4 AI channel comparison against organic, with the undercount caveat.
Add survey AI share, bot-log top pages, and GSC and Bing figures month over month.
Add crawlability status, mention pipeline status, and the single biggest gap for next month.

test.method: Confirm no raw citation count appears as the report's headline.

title: Run the GEO vendor vetting workflow before signing a contract
hypothesis: If the 5 questions, 3 probes, case-study band audit, content-volume check and prohibited-tactics screen all run in 1 vetting pass, then a hire or no-hire decision comes with real evidence instead of a gut call.

signal.check: A GEO agency or tool proposal is on the table with no completed vetting sheet.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the vetting steps into 1 documented decision

steps: Ask the 5 questions and 3 probes on a call and record answers verbatim.
Ask for the case-study keyword list, split it by difficulty band, and check how the client performs now.
Ask whether the platform generates content and how many pages the plan publishes.
Walk through the prohibited-tactics list; any yes is a no-hire.
For a tracker, compare surfaces, prompt limits, pricing and logged-in support against 2 cheaper options.
Write the vetting sheet and the final decision.

test.method: Confirm the vetting sheet is complete before signing.

title: Run the AI-assisted drafting workflow without inventing facts
hypothesis: If drafting runs through a persistent workspace, source review, first-hand detail injection, hand-editing and real-photo conversion in 1 sequence, then pages draft faster without inventing a fact or a source.

signal.check: Content is being drafted with AI assistance and no structured review step for sources and facts exists.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this bundles the drafting steps into 1 controlled workflow

risk.note: Never bulk-publish; discard a draft rather than publish without a human edit.

steps: Add the brand brief and fact sheet as files in the persistent AI workspace.
Prompt for the capsule structure with topic, audience and goal.
Review every proposed source and reject anything not real or not relevant.
Inject first-hand product detail the assistant could not know.
Edit the draft by hand and check every fact against the fact sheet.
Convert any generated illustration to a real product photo where accuracy matters, add internal links and write the meta description.

test.method: Check every published page traces its facts to the fact sheet and carries a named editor.

title: Read the literal AI sub-queries behind a prompt with browser tools
hypothesis: If the literal sub-queries an assistant runs for a target prompt get read directly in the browser's network traffic, then real coverage gaps and phrasing get found instead of guessed, because fan-out phrasing usually differs from the user's original wording.

signal.check: A page brief needs to check topic coverage or borrow real phrasing but nobody has inspected the actual sub-queries the assistant ran.

expected_effect.size: unknown; this is an inspection technique and may stop working if the interface changes

risk.note: This is an undocumented browser technique that may break at any time; verify it still works before relying on it.

steps: In the assistant that shows search steps directly, read the sub-queries shown in the interface.
In another assistant, send the prompt, open developer tools, and find the network request while it is searching the web.
Copy the conversation identifier and filter network requests to find the matching entry.
Open the response and search for the query list inside it.
Record the sub-queries next to the prompt for coverage and phrasing, not as keyword targets.
Repeat periodically, since fan-out phrasing changes.

test.method: Compare the recorded sub-queries against the page's current section coverage.
